english.title: Knowingly withhold information to procure an established use certificate for town and country planning
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) for the purpose of procuring a particular decision on an application for the issue of an established use certificate under section 191 or 192 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, with intent to deceive, withheld information, namely **(..SPECIFY THE INFORMATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 194(1)(c) and (2) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 194(3) of the Act provides that notwithstanding section 127 of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980, a magistrates' court may try an information in respect this offence whenever laid.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
